translations.answer: In the G1/T1 settings of FALCON, the end-effector Jacobian, gravity torque, and joint torque are constrained in three-dimensional disturbances, and their scale is gradually expanded in conjunction with a shared proprioceptive upper and lower-body strategy. This approach yields lower force-tracking errors compared to force-torque perception, upper-body PD/IK, and same-stack single-body RL in real-world scenarios. The static approximation does not equal actual machine contact or thermal safety guarantees.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: End-effector Jacobians and joint torque limits are available in simulation.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Lower-body locomotion and upper-body joint tracking form separable objectives with shared proprioception.
translations.applicability.environments.0: 252 ACCAD targets under three force levels
translations.confidence_rationale: Controlled force-level, architecture and torque-aware curriculum comparisons plus a small real-robot quantitative test and public implementation support the mechanism. Confidence is capped by limited real quantitative scope and approximate force feasibility.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines force feasibility and compares dual-agent, monolithic, IK/PD and curriculum variants.
translations.evidence.0.title: FALCON: Learning Force-Adaptive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
translations.evidence.1.note: Maps torque-aware force and curriculum mechanisms to official code.
translations.evidence.1.title: LeCAR-Lab/FALCON official implementation
translations.safety.command_limits: Before hardware use, derive robot- and firmware-specific position, velocity, torque and contact-force limits; paper training clips are not deployment limits.
translations.safety.emergency_stop: Before force interaction, test an independent human-accessible emergency stop and verify stopping at the selected low-energy envelope.
translations.safety.protective_controls: Use a cleared exclusion zone, secured load, compatible fall protection, thermal/current monitoring, and a human safety operator.
translations.safety.robot_specific_warning: Evidence covers only the reported Unitree G1 and Booster T1 configurations; actuator, wrist, hand and SDK differences require a new review.
translations.safety.staged_deployment: Proceed from fixed-seed simulation to cross-simulator replay, supported no-contact motion, low-force single-axis contact, then bounded multi-axis tasks with logged abort criteria.
